packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-12 - blind first reading (unverified image reading)

Exposure: no proposed identification of the text was in my context before reading. The images themselves carry later labels (see survey) that I report as observations only.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, reduced overview)
- A single narrow vertical strip of parchment (approx. 4.5-5 cm wide x 19 cm tall by the scale at right), photographed on black with a colour checker. Likely a binding strip / spine lining reused from a codex; the text runs horizontally across the strip, so only a narrow slice of each written line survives (a few words per line, cut on both sides).
- Top: a modern paper label in blue ink "III C/L, 29" (shelfmark-like), with small pencilled notes to its right. Below it, in brown ink on the strip, a later inscription "Mar- / tialis" (looks like a spine title written on the strip when it served as a spine covering), and below that a small pencil note ("Gains/Gams? ..." and "...56" - not legible at overview scale).
- Main text: ca. 20+ lines of a small Gothic textualis/cursiva-like book hand in brown ink, visible from roughly the 1/4 point down to ca. 3/4 of the strip. A darker vertical crease/stain runs down the middle (spine fold). Lower part is damaged (holes, losses), then a further block of 2-3 lines at the bottom edge, more legible, possibly a different area of the leaf.
- Script appears to be in German vernacular rather than Latin at first glance (forms like "vnd" seem visible), to be checked on tiles.
- No rubrics or enlarged initials visible at overview scale. One column fragment only; original column width/ruling not recoverable from this strip.

TILE image-002.jpg (top of strip, native resolution)
Labels (observations): blue ink paper label "III C/L, 29" with pencil "Fng. / 15 Jh"(?) at right; brown ink later inscription "Mar- / tialis" across the strip (spine-title type, sits over/under faded text); blue pencil "Stams, STA Fng. / 15 Jh"(?) below it. These are later shelf/catalogue annotations, not part of the main text; I do not use them to identify anything.
Main text: small brown-ink German(?) cursive bookhand, very faded under a broad central brown/grey stain; each line cut at both edges, so only ~3-5 words per line. Lines numbered from the first text line under the labels (ca. 1/3 down the tile).

Note (image-002): readings on this tile are very low-confidence; the ink is largely abraded under the stain and the right portion of each line is lost in a dark band. Language judged German from "vnd", "nicht", "also", "selber" but even these are tentative.

SECOND FACE: image-004.jpg (reduced overview), image-005.jpg and image-006.jpg (tiles, top and bottom, overlapping in the middle)
- This is the reverse (pasted-down side) of the same strip. It shows no visible script: the surface is covered by a central band of brown leather/adhesive residue with spine-like impressions (horizontal bands at intervals, consistent with sewing supports), framed by two vertical lines (turn-ins or creases), and the side margins are covered with white fibrous paper/paste residue. Top and bottom ends are folded-over flaps.
- Only writing: modern pencil on the left margin, running upward, "Stams, STA, Fng. 156v" (image-006, lower left). Observation only.
- No text transcribed from this face; nothing legible through the residue in these images.
- image-007.jpg does not exist; the packet is image-001 to image-006.

LIMITATIONS
- Packet = image-001 (overview, text face), image-002/003 (text-face tiles), image-004 (overview, reverse), image-005/006 (reverse tiles). All viewed once; no crops made.
- The strip preserves only a narrow middle slice of each line; both ends cut. The central stain/abrasion makes most middle words illegible; nearly every reading carries a question mark.
- Language appears to be Middle High German / Early New High German prose (vnd, nicht, also, selber, sprechen, Sy waren, wol), cursive bookhand; this is an observation, not a dating.
- Areas read: all text lines on both tiles, at low confidence. Unread / effectively illegible: the centre of nearly every line. A raking-light or UV image, or a contrast-enhanced crop of the central band, would be needed; the bottom flap (l.19-22) would also benefit from unfolding/separate imaging. The reverse face (image-004 to 006) carries no visible text under the binding residue.
- The later inscription "Martialis" and the shelf labels are visible in the images; I report them only as observations and did not use them for any identification.
- I did nothing beyond the brief's rules.
